renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Flowers first, all in order — emblem or altar; with fourteen mutterings, prepare the flower-seat. There let the hero worship the forthgoing, then the seat again; casketed, let him start the worship after.

Full of all realities, graced with all ornaments — let the great lady worship the twenty-seven-named goddess. Then with fragrant flowers, as able, honor; worship with supreme devotion, and give yourself away.

Thus worship told; in fire-rite too this rule: who did the worship, rightly recalling the seed, succeeds. Beginningless-endless seed, abloom, gone mid-moon-days, housed in the heart-lotus — meditate the moon-ray, practise always.

Whatever he desires, swiftly he gains; from this he goes to direct sight — all-knowingness, no doubt. Thus mantra-fruit is got — this is Rudra's Pair-book; by its practice, powers stay and all-knowing stays.

paragraphs.text: Flowers up front, all lined up — emblem or altar; fourteen mutterings in, build the flower-seat. Hero worships the forthgoing there, then the seat again; boxed up, on with the worship.
All-truths-full, all-ornaments-graced — let lady luck worship the twenty-seven-named goddess. Fragrant flowers per budget, worship with max love, and hand yourself over.

Worship: told. Fire-rite too, same rule: done the worship, seed on mind, win. Seed with no start or end, blooming mid-moon-days, heart-lotus-housed — moon-ray on loop. What he wants, wants, lands fast; direct sight from this — all-knowing, no doubt.
Mantra-fruit: got. This is Rudra's Pair-book; run the practice and powers plus all-knowing stick around.
